receipts.scope: Workflow 8 adds complex current spectra and grouped time and frequency exports from accepted configuration and operating-point pairs.
conventions: The spectrum uses uniform samples and coherent-gain-corrected one-sided peak amplitudes. DC and even-length Nyquist retain unit multiplicity. The odd-length final bin keeps multiplicity two.
Phase in radians uses atan2 and the first sample as its reference. An exactly zero phasor has null phase. The full spectrum and Parseval evidence remain available.

The first ten bins in ascending frequency with magnitude strictly greater than peak times relative_threshold qualify. The default fraction is 0.1. A threshold of 1 or an all-zero signal yields no selected bins.
The time export distinguishes arithmetic sample mean, sample standard deviation with N minus one denominator, and discrete RMS from piecewise-linear time mean and RMS.
The grouped export covers each supplied current, gate voltage, device voltage and bus voltage. It retains source, configuration, operating point, weight, SI unit, statuses, error and input hashes.
Unrequested spectra, unsupported operations and computed spectra with no retained bins have distinct manifest evidence. The grid preserves failed pairs and applies no phase averaging.

receipts.scope: Workflow 9 compares complete waveform-grid configurations using one to four declared power objectives.
conventions: Operating-point weights determine each raw full mean in W. Every active objective uses the same complete configuration population.
Positive objective weights determine relative contributions to the dimensionless score. A zero objective weight contributes zero and leaves the configuration eligible.
Minimization penalizes the distance above the population minimum. Maximization penalizes the distance below the maximum. Both divide by the full range. A constant range gives zero penalty.
Lower scores rank first. Equal computed scores share a competition rank. Configuration IDs order each tie. Each extreme lists every tied configuration.
Excluded active objectives retain null penalties and contributions. Missing positive-weight points remain identifiable even when the reported coverage rounds to one.
The server rejects a positive normalized weight, penalty or contribution that would round to zero. It constrains the score to the observed range of active penalties.

review_export.opt_in: Add objectives to the grid request. An absent or null objectives field preserves the original request hash and response.
review_export.downloads: The browser downloads the complete JSON array or CSV table returned by the server. Every row retains both hashes, population IDs, direction, weights, raw mean, extrema, coverage and contribution.

independent_checks: The A and B power fixtures give conduction means of 25 W and 20 W and turn-on means of 4 W and 8 W. Minimize weights of 1 and 3 give scores of 0.25 and 0.75.
For minimize ranges from 0 to 2 W, a middle mean of 5e-324 W would yield a false zero penalty. A separate positive contribution can also underflow. Both cases fail explicitly.
Three unit penalties with objective weights 0.01, 0.01 and 4 give exactly 1. The complete fixture gives ranks 1, 1 and 3.
A missing point with weight 1e-30 leaves rounded coverage at 1. The incomplete configuration remains excluded and retains null contributions in JSON and CSV.
A 32-configuration fixture with four constant objectives preserves all 128 audit rows and all tied Unicode identifiers in JSON and CSV.

limitations: These calculated fixtures verify the declared comparison policy. Device measurement accuracy needs independent physical evidence.
Rounding can cause a last-digit difference between a score and the sum of exported contributions. A conservative metadata estimate can reject long identities before export.

receipts.scope: Workflow 10 binds one converter calculation to explicit physical members, die owners, junction owners and independent ideal-fixed-sink paths.
conventions: The wrapper evaluates the converter once. Per-member values are not multiplied by role multiplicity again.
Conduction and switching currents remain independent. Positive, negative and finite zero-current events use explicit owners.
Die and junction ownership are independent. Negative current can belong to a channel. A shared junction requires the same explicit ID.
Physical-owner energies are aggregated before division by duration. Unknown or omitted loss remains null. Empty known subtotals do not become fabricated zero.
Known heat remains available without a thermal path. Full temperature requires sourced paths, heat coverage and complete physical inventory.
The full maximum retains all tied hottest junctions. Acknowledged known-heat-only temperature remains separate from full temperature.
The boundary is an ideal fixed sink with constant heat. Iteration is not-required-constant-heat. No shared-sink rise, electrothermal feedback or Foster transient is claimed.
Canonical request and converter SHA-256 identify normalized inputs. The nullable upstream digest is caller-declared and not verified against source bytes.
